summary: Wayne Hathaway's comments on the new Telnet protocol and option specifications. He thinks they are far better than before but objects to details, especially the notes on option subnegotiation and how Telnet SYNCH is handled when there is more than one Telnet interpreter. RFC 529 replies.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reviews new Telnet rules and praises the overall direction while identifying unclear details. Its main concern is how a receiver should find the end of special parameters and process a SYNCH.

subtitle: Comments on the proposed Telnet protocol and option specifications.

tldr.problem: Wayne Hathaway found unclear details in proposed Telnet specifications, especially how subnegotiation and SYNCH should be handled.
tldr.mechanism: He proposes explicit subnegotiation boundaries, consistent escaping of IAC bytes, a narrower definition of SYNCH scanning, and several editorial clarifications.
tldr.outcome: RFC 513 is a set of review comments, not a specification. RFC 529 later responds to its discussion of SYNCH.

sections.title: Review of the New Telnet Rules
sections.content: Wayne Hathaway comments on the proposed Telnet Protocol Specification and Telnet Option Specification. He considers the new protocol much better than the earlier version but recommends changes to some substantive points and editorial wording.
sections.plainLanguage: The author supports the new specifications overall. He asks for clearer instructions in several important places.

sections.title: Subnegotiation and SYNCH
sections.content:
Hathaway objects to statements that assume each party can parse option subnegotiation parameters and that an IAC byte inside them need not be doubled. If a user process handles the parameters, the Network Control Program may not know how to scan them during a Telnet SYNCH.

He proposes explicit parameter endings and requiring parameters to follow general Telnet rules, including doubling IAC. He also suggests limiting the signals recognized during a SYNCH scan to the Data Mark command.
sections.plainLanguage: Every receiver needs to know exactly where special parameters end. Hathaway says the rules should make that boundary clear so a SYNCH scan can work reliably.

sections.title: Other Proposed Clarifications
sections.content:
The author suggests changes to how the specifications describe a SYNCH, Abort Output, print position, the word promptly, and the CR-NUL convention. He also asks for a way to specify horizontal tab positions and use.

For a SYNCH, he proposes discarding input up to and including the next Data Mark command, and discusses possible ways to indicate that the scan has completed.
sections.plainLanguage: The remaining comments ask the specification to explain several commands and conventions more precisely. They also raise the need for a way to describe horizontal tab stops.
